tags.gist: Draws drug-safety lessons: postmarket systems detect only prespecified harms, depend on record quality, and tend to count timeliness rather than detection capability.
Would accept the trade only if sponsors state which failure classes monitoring detects and misses, the detection interval, and how claims are verified in operation.
Calls sample-based clinician review the right instinct but says it assumes adjudicator agreement that vague criteria like clinically appropriate do not deliver.
Wants review criteria written as decision rules spelling out which evidence yields a yes or a no, and what to do when evidence is absent.
Wants a share of samples reviewed by more than one adjudicator, with agreement reported against a prespecified acceptable range.
Wants adjudicators calibrated through periodic joint review of standardized cases, and recalibrated after model, criteria or panel changes.
Wants each adjudication reconstructable, recording what was examined, against which source and on what basis, not only the outcome.
Suggests triggers: any model or architecture change including upstream ones, detected drift, input-population change, and accumulated adjudicator divergence.
Asks who answers when a supervisor errs, wanting a defined context of use, failure-weighted validation, its own drift monitoring, recorded human override and version provenance.
Cautions that automation suits deterministic checks, not the clinical judgment sample review exists for, so throughput should not be reported as assurance.
Would separate roles by function: societies build adjudicator calibration libraries, institutions own frictionless reporting pathways, manufacturers keep the monitoring programme.
Notes a confident wrong output may not register as a reportable malfunction at complaint intake, and asks for guidance on what counts for generative functions.
Concludes monitoring can carry premarket weight only when specified with equal rigor, including candor about what it cannot detect and measured adjudicator agreement.

skipped.reason: Mentions the writer's own prototype toolkit, not offered as a solution.
